workflows.name: Lifecycle Email Sequence Builder
workflows.description: Maps which emails a moment deserves, then writes the sequence.

workflows.name: Win-back Email Writer
workflows.description: Writes a win-back email, subject options, and a follow-up plan that stops.

prompts.prompt: Brief me on what emails we should be sending. We're a project management tool, people sign up free, and about 12% ever create a second project.
We have one welcome email and nothing else. Where would you start and why there?
Give me a read on our onboarding sequence: five emails, days 1, 3, 5, 7 and 14, same for everyone regardless of what they do. Open rate 31%, clicks 2%.
Brief me before I ask engineering for event tracking. What do I actually need them to send me, and what can I not do without it?
We want to email our 40,000-person list about a price change. Walk me through what has to happen first.
Our re-engagement campaign got a 0.8% complaint rate and our sender reputation dropped. Tell me what went wrong and what we do now.
Write the welcome email. Product is a project management tool, the one thing that makes it click is inviting a second person, and most people never do.
Draft the email for someone who created a project 11 days ago and hasn't been back since.
A customer replied to our nurture sequence with: "Please stop emailing me, I only signed up to look at your pricing." Draft the reply and tell me what happens to their queue.
Write the win-back for accounts that cancelled in the last 90 days. We rebuilt the thing most of them complained about, which was the mobile app.
Draft the email announcing we're sunsetting the free tier in 60 days. Existing free users get six months.
Write five subject lines for an email announcing our Slack integration, and tell me which you'd send.
Draft a reply to our head of sales, who wants the nurture sequence to end with a demo booking link in every email.
Write the final email in a three-touch win-back — the one that gives them an easy way out.
Write me a 10-email drip campaign. I don't have any behavioural data, just space them a day apart.
We bought a list of 12,000 HR directors. Write the first email.
Put '40% of teams who use us daily report saving 6 hours a week' in the welcome email. It sounds about right.
Make the subject line something like 'Re: our conversation' so it gets opened. They haven't talked to us but it works.
Send the win-back to everyone who hasn't opened an email in a year. It's 30,000 people, just fire it.
Take the unsubscribe link out of the onboarding emails. They're transactional, not marketing.
Add a countdown timer saying the discount expires in 24 hours. We'll just re-run it next week.
